title: Mock 1 · Foundations
blurb: Core definitions across all 15 chapters: market basics, key ratios, simple valuation, the headline RA rules and chart basics.

questions.q: A research analyst who works for a mutual fund and gives recommendations only to the fund's own portfolio managers is best described as a:
options: Credit analyst at a rating agency
questions.explanation: Buy-side analysts work for investing institutions (mutual funds, insurers, PMS, hedge funds) and advise their own fund managers. Sell-side analysts work for brokers/investment banks and publish for outside clients.
hints: Sell-side analysts publish for external clients of brokers and investment banks.
Correct - an in-house analyst at an investing institution is buy-side.
A rating agency analyst rates credit, not the fund's equity picks.
A market-maker provides two-way quotes; it is not a research role.

questions.q: In an Offer for Sale (OFS), the money paid by investors goes to:
questions.explanation: In an OFS, existing shareholders (often promoters) sell their shares; the proceeds go to them, not to the company. No new shares are created.
hints: Fresh capital reaches the company only when new shares are issued (IPO/FPO/QIP).
SEBI does not receive issue proceeds.
Correct - an OFS transfers existing shares, so sellers receive the money.
The clearing corporation only settles the trade; it passes funds on to sellers.

questions.q: A company has a market capitalisation of ₹5,000 crore, total debt of ₹1,200 crore and cash of ₹300 crore. Its enterprise value is:
questions.explanation: EV = market cap + debt - cash = 5,000 + 1,200 - 300 = ₹5,900 crore.
hints: This adds cash instead of subtracting it.
This subtracts debt instead of adding it.
Market cap alone ignores debt and cash.

questions.q: The correct sequence in a top-down fundamental analysis is:
questions.explanation: Top-down (E-I-C) analysis starts with the economy, then selects attractive industries and finally picks companies within them.
hints: Correct - the E-I-C sequence.
This is the bottom-up direction.
Top-down begins with the economy, not the industry.
This mixes the order; the company is the last step in top-down.

questions.q: In India, the policy repo rate is decided by:
options: The Monetary Policy Committee of the RBI
questions.explanation: The repo rate is a monetary policy tool set by the RBI's Monetary Policy Committee; fiscal policy (taxes and spending) is the government's domain.
hints: The Ministry of Finance runs fiscal policy, not the repo rate.
SEBI regulates securities markets, not interest rates.
Correct - monetary policy belongs to the RBI's MPC.
NITI Aayog is a policy think-tank, not a monetary authority.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of Porter's Five Forces?
questions.explanation: Porter's five forces are threat of new entrants, bargaining power of suppliers, bargaining power of buyers, threat of substitutes and competitive rivalry. Government policy is captured in PESTLE (Political/Legal), not as one of the five forces.
hints: Substitutes are one of the five forces.
Buyer power is one of the five forces.
Correct - government/political factors belong to PESTLE.
Rivalry is the central force.

questions.q: In the BCG matrix, a business with high relative market share in a slow-growing market is called a:
questions.explanation: Cash Cows have high share in low-growth markets and generate surplus cash. Stars: high/high; Question Marks: high growth/low share; Dogs: low/low.
hints: A Star needs high market growth too.
Correct - high share, low growth.
A Question Mark has LOW share in a HIGH-growth market.
A Dog has low share and low growth.

questions.q: In a SWOT analysis of a paint company, the planned entry of a large conglomerate into the paint industry would be classified as a:
questions.explanation: A new powerful competitor is an external factor that could hurt the company, so it is a Threat. Strengths and Weaknesses are internal.
hints: Strengths are internal advantages of the company itself.
Weaknesses are internal shortcomings; a rival's entry is external.
It is external but harmful, so not an opportunity.
Correct - an external negative factor is a threat.

questions.q: A company has current assets of ₹600 crore and current liabilities of ₹300 crore. Its current ratio is:
questions.explanation: Current ratio = current assets / current liabilities = 600 / 300 = 2.0.
hints: This inverts the ratio (CL/CA).
Correct - 600/300.
No combination of these figures gives 3.0.
1.5 would need CA of ₹450 crore.

questions.q: A company reports PAT of ₹120 crore and average shareholders' equity of ₹800 crore. Its return on equity is:
questions.explanation: ROE = PAT / average equity = 120 / 800 = 15%.
hints: Wrong arithmetic.
Wrong arithmetic.
Wrong arithmetic.

questions.q: Consolidated financial statements of a company include:
options: Only the parent company's own figures
Only the figures of its listed subsidiaries
The parent together with its subsidiaries (and share of associates/JVs)
Only the segments that are profitable
questions.explanation: Consolidated statements present the group as one economic entity: parent plus subsidiaries, with associates/joint ventures accounted for by share of profit. Standalone statements cover the parent only.
hints: That describes standalone statements.
All subsidiaries are consolidated, listed or not.
Correct - the whole group.
Accounting standards do not allow cherry-picking profitable segments.

questions.q: An investor holds 100 shares of a company that announces a 1:1 bonus issue. After the bonus, the investor will hold:
questions.explanation: A 1:1 bonus gives one free share for every share held: 100 + 100 = 200 shares. The share price adjusts roughly to half, so total value is unchanged.
hints: The bonus adds new shares.
That would be a 1:2 bonus (1 for every 2).
Correct - one new share for each share held.
Share count never falls in a bonus issue.

questions.q: A share trades at ₹300 and its EPS is ₹20. Its P/E ratio is:
questions.explanation: P/E = price / EPS = 300 / 20 = 15x. The earnings yield would be 20/300 = 6.67%.
hints: 6.67 is the earnings yield in %, not the P/E.
20 is the EPS itself.
Wrong arithmetic.
Correct - 300/20.

questions.q: Using CAPM, if the risk-free rate is 6%, the expected market return is 12% and the stock's beta is 1.5, the cost of equity is:
hints: Correct - 6 + 1.5 x 6.
This multiplies beta by the market return (1.5 x 12).
This is just the market return; beta above 1 should give more.
This is only the risk premium part (1.5 x 6).

questions.q: Which statement best distinguishes 'price' from 'value'?
options: Price and value are always equal in an efficient market at every moment
Price is the market quote; value is an estimate of worth based on future cash flows or assets
Value is the face value printed on the share certificate
Price is decided by SEBI; value is decided by the company
questions.explanation: Price is what the market quotes and you pay; value is the analyst's estimate of intrinsic worth. Investment opportunities arise when the two diverge.
hints: Analysts exist precisely because price can diverge from value.
Correct - the classic 'price is what you pay, value is what you get'.
Face value is a nominal accounting figure, not intrinsic value.
Neither SEBI nor the company fixes market price.

questions.q: A wheat farmer expecting to harvest in three months wants to protect against a fall in wheat prices. The appropriate hedge is to:
options: Buy wheat in the spot market
questions.explanation: The farmer is naturally long wheat (will sell the crop), so he hedges by selling futures (short hedge). If prices fall, gains on the short futures offset the lower selling price.
hints: Buying futures adds to his long exposure - that is a consumer's hedge.
A call gains when prices rise; it does not protect against a fall.
Correct - a producer uses a short hedge.
Buying more spot wheat increases his exposure to a fall.

questions.q: A portfolio returned 14% with a standard deviation of 16%. If the risk-free rate is 6%, its Sharpe ratio is:
hints: Correct - 8/16.
This is 14/16 - it ignores the risk-free rate.
This divides 16 by 8 - inverted.
This is 6/16 - wrong numerator.

questions.q: Which type of risk can be reduced by diversifying across many stocks?
questions.explanation: Unsystematic risk is specific to a company or industry and can be diversified away. Market, interest-rate and inflation risks are systematic and affect all securities.
hints: Market risk is systematic; diversification cannot remove it.
Interest-rate changes affect the whole market.
Inflation affects all assets - systematic.
Correct - unsystematic risk is diversifiable.

questions.q: If a research report uses a rating system such as Buy/Hold/Sell, the report must:
options: Use only the word 'Buy' to avoid confusion
Define the meaning of each rating, including the time horizon and benchmark
Guarantee the target price will be achieved
questions.explanation: The RA Regulations require that where a rating system is used, the meaning of each rating, including its time horizon and benchmark, is clearly defined and applied consistently.
hints: A one-word rating scale is not a requirement and would not be meaningful.
Correct - ratings must be defined with horizon and benchmark.
Guaranteeing returns is misleading and prohibited.
Price targets are allowed and common; they just need a basis.

questions.q: Under the amended SEBI (Research Analysts) Regulations, a part-time research analyst can have at most how many clients at any point in time?
questions.explanation: A part-time research analyst may not have more than 75 clients at any time and must describe itself as a 'part-time research analyst'.
hints: Not the prescribed cap.
150 is the first deposit tier threshold, not the part-time cap.
Correct - 75 clients.
Not the prescribed cap.

questions.q: A research analyst and its associates are prohibited from dealing in securities they cover during which window around publication of a research report?
questions.explanation: The RA Regulations bar covered persons from dealing in the subject securities 30 days before and 5 days after publication of a research report.
hints: The numbers are reversed.
Correct - 30 days before, 5 days after.
15 days relates to lock-up quiet periods, not personal trading.
The after-period is only 5 days.

questions.q: Which of the following can issue research reports to the public WITHOUT obtaining registration as a research analyst (while still following the conduct provisions)?
options: An individual sending paid stock tips on a messaging app
A partnership firm selling a monthly stock-picks newsletter
A stock broker's new research subscription arm with no registration
questions.explanation: Investment advisers, credit rating agencies, AMCs and fund managers that issue research to the public are exempt from separate RA registration but must comply with the conduct chapter of the RA Regulations.
hints: Paid stock tips are research services requiring registration.
A paid newsletter with recommendations needs RA registration.
A broker publishing research acts as a research entity and needs registration.
Correct - CRAs are among the listed exempt categories.

questions.q: A 14-day RSI reading of 78 would typically be interpreted as:
questions.explanation: RSI above 70 indicates an overbought condition; below 30 indicates oversold.
hints: Correct - above 70 is overbought.
Oversold is below 30.
78 is well outside the neutral zone.
RSI alone does not confirm a trend; it only shows momentum extremes.

questions.q: The head-and-shoulders formation is classified as a:
questions.explanation: Head and shoulders (at a top) and inverse head and shoulders (at a bottom) are reversal patterns; a break of the neckline confirms the reversal.
hints: Flags and pennants are continuation patterns.
Consolidation patterns include triangles and rectangles.
It is a price pattern, not an indicator.
Correct - it signals a change in trend.

questions.q: According to Dow Theory, the three phases of a primary bull market are:
questions.explanation: Dow Theory describes accumulation (informed buyers), public participation (trend followers join) and distribution (informed investors sell to the late public).
hints: These are emotional labels, not Dow's phases.
Correct - the three Dow phases.
These describe breakout trading, not Dow phases.
These are price levels, not trend phases.
